carousels.name: A morning routine that protects your night

slides.title: You don't relapse at night. You lose it [[in the morning.]]
slides.sub: The first hour of your day decides how strong you are at 1 AM.

slides.title: No phone for [[30 minutes]]
slides.body: Starting the day scrolling sets your brain up for cheap hits all day long. Give it 30 minutes of quiet first.

slides.title: Get [[sunlight]] and move
slides.body: A short walk outside, some stretching, a quick workout. Many people say it's the single habit that made their evenings calmer.

slides.title: Decide [[tonight]] now
slides.body: Write one line: "Tonight I will ___ instead." A plan made at 8 AM beats a decision made at midnight.

carousels.name: P*rn is quietly wrecking your confidence

slides.title: P*rn is quietly [[wrecking your confidence.]]
slides.sub: The comparison trap nobody warns you about.

slides.title: You're comparing to [[fiction]]
slides.body: Edited, scripted, performed. Measuring yourself against it is like comparing your body to a superhero movie.

slides.title: The [[shame]] tax
slides.body: Hiding something every day wears you down. Many people say they felt lighter — and stood taller — once they stopped.

slides.title: Confidence is [[earned]]
slides.body: Every promise you keep to yourself is a deposit. Every relapse you hide is a withdrawal. Start making deposits.

slides.title: Rebuild it [[daily]]
items: Keep one small promise to yourself every day.
Train your body for how it feels, not how it looks.
Talk to real people — awkward is fine.
Unfollow anything that makes you feel smaller.
slides.note: Has quitting changed how you see yourself? Share below 👇

slides.title:
Stop comparing.
[[Start rebuilding.]]
slides.lead: Learn the truth about p*rn's effects, block it completely and track every day you keep your word.

carousels.name: 4 lies p*rn taught you about real relationships

slides.title: 4 lies p*rn taught you about [[real relationships.]]
slides.sub: #3 ruins more relationships than you'd think.

slides.title: Lies [[1–2]]
items: "Intimacy is a performance." Real connection is about trust, not a show.
"Everyone looks like that." Real bodies are normal. The screen isn't.

slides.title: "Consent is [[obvious.]]"
slides.body: Real people communicate, check in and say what they want. Asking isn't awkward. It's respect — and it's attractive.

slides.title: "More [[novelty]] = more happiness."
slides.body: Endless novelty trains you to always want the next thing. Depth with one person is a different, better kind of good.

slides.title: Real is [[better]].
slides.body: Real relationships are slower, messier and more human. Many people in recovery say that's exactly what makes them worth it.
slides.note: Which lie did you believe the longest? Comment the number 👇

slides.title:
Unlearn the screen.
[[Learn real connection.]]
slides.lead: Quick guides about p*rn and its effects, plus an anonymous community going through the same thing.

slides.title: Should you date [[while you're quitting?]]
slides.sub: What people in recovery wish they'd known earlier.

slides.title: You don't need to be [["fixed"]] first
slides.body: Waiting until you're perfect can mean waiting forever. But be honest with yourself about where you are.

slides.title: A partner is [[not]] a cure
slides.body: A relationship won't make the habit disappear. If you're dating to escape, that's the same pattern in a new outfit.

slides.title: Real dates [[train]] your brain
slides.body: Eye contact, conversation, real attraction. Many people say real-world dating helped them reconnect with what they actually want.

slides.title: Date the [[healthy]] way
items: Don't hide your recovery once it gets serious.
Keep your support system — don't replace it.
slides.note: Dating while quitting: helpful or harder? Tell us 👇

slides.title:
Show up as
[[the real you.]]

slides.title: 20 push-ups can beat an urge [[better than willpower.]]
slides.sub: Why moving your body is one of the strongest tools you have.

slides.title: It burns the [[restlessness]]
slides.body: Urges often feel like restless energy with nowhere to go. Movement gives it somewhere to go — fast.

slides.title: It changes your [[state]]
slides.body: Many people report feeling calmer and more in control after even a short workout. A different state means a different decision.

slides.title: It builds [[proof]]
slides.body: Every workout is evidence that you can do hard things. That proof shows up at 1 AM when you need it.
